cards.note: Black car can be hard to see depending on the driving surface. It is quite sparse and doesn't appear often. (see second image for an example of black car)
no car no antenna is the most common gen 4 car and appears in many places.

Gen 4 no car with antenna is sparse. Most prominently it covers the long road between Yaroslavl - Kirov - Perm - Chelyabinsk.

While quite reliable, the antenna sometimes can be blurred out and it appears like 'no car no antenna' - that's just bad luck for you then :(
Red car is usually easier to recognize than black or white car

White car can be hard to see and probably takes some practice to spot, sometimes it just isn't really visible. It mostly appears in the far east in Sakha and Magadan which are luckily quite recognizable by vibes. (see third image for an example of white car)
Seasons can help to further narrow down your guess

Does not include white car long antenna, which is also mainly a-type pronounced. White car long antenna is covered seperately to keep things a bit more simple.

Long a-type pronounced is also referred to as 'long very a-type'
This type is quite sparse and appears only around Yaroslavl, Ivanovo and Vladimir

No seasonal metas here, all summer. (Just a few exceptions with september coverage around moscow)

Long b-type pronounced is also referred to as 'long very b type'
Seasons can help to further narrow down your guess

B-type is the most common type of short antenna.

Learning camera smudge metas can be especially helpful for b-type:

YT tutorial by SwordSlicer56

Google doc by Illusion

B-type pronounced, also referred to as 'very b-type' can sometimes be confused with normal b-type. To differenciate the two it helps to know that b-type pronounced will never have smudges, which normal b-type has a lot.
The second most common type of short antenna

Blurred tilted is either around st. petersburg or around volgograd, which looks so different that it is a easy 50/50. You don't get blurred tilted often. To be sure of the tilt line up the antenna with the bottom middle of your screen, you then should be able to see the tilt to the left.
The third most common type of short antenna

This one is quite region-guessable through seasonal metas, although a bit less common in appearance. To be sure of the tilt line up the antenna with the bottom middle of your screen, you then should be able to see the tilt to the left.
